source.title: Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models
source.authors: Luke Leckie; Peter M. Todd; Jacob G. Foster

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures concept-level activations before their later verbalisation during semantic fluency, using J-lens analyses rather than the rhyme-word method in the claim. It also intervenes on activations, but does not test rhyme planning or whether features are computed specifically for later positions rather than as a byproduct of next-token prediction.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior rhyme-planning work as background; it does not reproduce or test that result. J-space depletion and generic switch-prediction results concern semantic switching, not whether a particular future token is represented, so they are not included as rows for these versions. Steering results that directly bias category switches are recorded as findings not covered by a version.
record.test_reason: In a new task (animal semantic fluency), J-lens activations of category labels rise over several items before the model switches into that category. This bears on look-ahead beyond verse (V5). The item-level rows compare switch and cluster items only at the position immediately before emission, so they concern next-token uncertainty, not future-token decodability (V2). The authors do not frame any of this as planning.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add that the authors leave open whether the dynamics extend to frontier models, and whether the human-LLM parallels are superficial or reflect deeper convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies J-lens measurements and residual-stream steering to semantic fluency in animal lists, rather than testing the cited rhyme-planning method. It also uses generic switch-direction steering.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported effects depend on model and layer. J-space depletion effects were most salient in middle layers and varied by model; category-label steering was generally strongest in middle or mid-to-late layers, item-level steering tended to strengthen toward later layers, and generic steering potency varied across models and layers.

fits_no_version.finding: At lag -1, J-lens activations of the next item are lower for switch items than for cluster items, from early-middle layers up.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In semantic fluency, intermediate layers encode lower next-item confidence before category switches.

fits_no_version.finding: Item-level, category-label and generic switch-direction steering biases category switching.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream directions associated with categories or switching causally bias explore/exploit switching in semantic fluency.

record.problems: The models are relatively small instruction-tuned models, and the authors say it is unknown whether the dynamics extend to frontier models, naturalistic speech, or other search tasks. Llama-3.1-8B did not have a precomputed J-lens, so J-lens experiments were not run for it. Some results are presented as aggregate significance statements or figures rather than individual effect sizes.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Rhyme planning in a frontier model; not studied.
No decoding accuracy for tokens several positions ahead; the item comparisons are at lag -1 only.
Whether features are computed for the benefit of later positions.
Whether the anticipatory label representation steers output several items later; steering was tested only on the immediately next item. Chess, Sokoban and multi-step reasoning not tested.
No test of whether the anticipation is explained by local features or heuristics.

missing.what: Lag-by-lag anticipation statistics (target minus unrelated label) before the switch, per model; needed to judge how far ahead the anticipation reaches.
Raw rise in item activation at earlier lags before emission (Fig. 2B, S1A); no numbers reported.

record.verdict_notes: The record's problems field wrongly says Llama-3.1-8B lacked a J-lens; the text says Llama-3.2-3B ('Llama-3B') lacked one, and J-lens results are reported for Llama-8B. Unrelated labels also rise before switches, though less than target labels, so the anticipation is relative. The study's framing is semantic foraging, not planning.

versions.untested_parts: Rhyme-word representations and interventions that change intervening verse to fit a different rhyme ending.
The study measures anticipation of later SFT items and category labels, not general token-prediction accuracy across tasks or architectures.
Whether features are computed because they benefit later positions, rather than arising as a side effect of next-token prediction.
Rhyme planning in open-weight models and its detection with open attribution-graph or probing tools.
Look-ahead in multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or the other specified tasks and architectures.
Whether apparent planning is shallow or incidental, or whether local next-token features or heuristics explain it.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B
rows.operation_detail: Measured J-lens activations of items at positions preceding their emission; compared items in switches with items in clusters.

conditions.value: layers 2–40, every second layer; comparison reported from layer 8 up

rows.measure: J-lens activation of the item later verbalised
rows.value: Switch-participating item activations were lower before emission; activations of both switch- and cluster-participating items increased in anticipation of emission.
rows.uncertainty: LR, all models from layer 8 up: χ² ≥ 98.17, p < 0.0001; figure reports standard errors.
rows.note: The text reports the significance threshold across models and layers rather than a single aggregate effect size.
rows.check: Measured at lag -1, immediately before emission: a next-token switch-vs-cluster contrast, not decoding of tokens several positions ahead. Unlink from V2.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B
rows.operation_detail: Measured J-lens activations of category-related labels before and after switches into target versus unrelated categories.
rows.measure: Activation of category-related labels anticipating a switch into the corresponding category
rows.value: Target-category label activations progressively increased before switching into that category and spiked at the switch.
rows.uncertainty: At the switch into the target category, LR across all models: F ≥ 848.35, p < 0.0001; figure reports standard errors.
rows.note: The paper reports the aggregate pattern across labels and seeds, with layer-averaged activation curves.
rows.check: Should link to V5, not V2: label tokens are not the future tokens. The uncertainty given (F ≥ 848.35) is at lag 0, the switch itself. The anticipation evidence is lags -6 to -1, all significant (Table S6).

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.3; Figure 3B-D; Table S6, Gemma-9B: significant positive differences at every lag from -6 through -1.

relation.reason: The study measures anticipatory category representations during ordinary task generation and intervenes on category and switching directions.

tranche.reason: Animal semantic fluency is a new setting with direct results on anticipatory internal representations relevant to V5.

source_check.notes: Category-label activations are not predictions of the exact future emitted tokens. The reported F ≥ 848.35 concerns the switch event, not the multi-item anticipation; generalization to frontier models and deeper human–LLM computational convergence remain open.

statements.correction: Table S6: Gemma-2-9B significant at lags -6 through -1; Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.1-8B significant at lags -5 through -1. Section 2: 100 seeds per model-layer combination. Section 3.4: item- and category-label steering changes the first continuation item's category. Section 4.2: generic-direction steering changes switching rates relative to noise controls. Multi-item anticipation itself is correlational.
statements.problem: The anticipation horizons and 100 seeds are correct, but describing this study as entirely correlational overlooks its category-specific and generic switching interventions.

statements.correction: Table S6, Qwen2.5-7B: significant positive anticipation at lag -6 (beta 0.208, p 5.09E-05) and lag -3 (beta 0.235, p 1.50E-07); non-significant at -5, -4, -2 and -1. Betas at -4, -2 and -1 are negative.
statements.problem: The listed negative-beta lags are correct, but the blanket claim of no significant anticipation in Qwen omits significant positive differences at two other anticipatory lags.

statements.correction: Section 3.4: category-directed steering is evaluated on the first concept in the continuation. Section 4.2: generic switching-direction steering is evaluated through switching rates. Neither experiment establishes that a localized intervention changes a specific represented future item several items later.
statements.problem: The missing localized delayed-output test is correctly identified, but the statement that steering was tested only on the immediately next item is too broad: the paper also tests generic steering effects on switching rates.
